Vagaro Rolls Out Smarter Med Spa Software to Connect Treatment Data With Revenue Share:

Vagaro, a widely used platform for medical spa, beauty, wellness, and fitness businesses, has rolled out new medical spa software upgrades aimed at turning everyday treatment data into measurable business value. The rollout centers on stronger SOAP Notes and Custom Fields, both built to be HIPAA compliant while tightening up clinical workflows across the platform. "Having access to all the information, transaction lists, and dashboards has helped us make critical business decisions throughout the quarters and years," said Bailey Ames, Co-Founder of Lash + Company, a leading med spa enterprise. As med spas scale up services, open new locations, and see growing patient volumes, documentation demands are climbing right along with them. Providers still need to move quickly without sacrificing accuracy or consistency. With nearly 4 million appointments booked through Vagaro so far this year, the company says it's building its updates directly around how providers actually work day to day. These latest changes tie together several stages of the patient journey — consultation, treatment documentation, product tracking, inventory, billing, and checkout — into one connected workflow, helping practices manage more information without sacrificing the patient experience. Upgraded SOAP Notes Bring More Depth to Treatment Documentation The revamped SOAP Notes give providers a more dynamic way to handle EMR charting. Practitioners can now capture before-and-after photos mid-treatment and use them to visually document procedures as they happen. Photos can be annotated to mark treatment areas, making it easier to flag injection points, laser zones, or spots needing follow-up. Providers can also tag products and quantities directly to specific areas in treatment images, creating a precise record of what was used where. That data flows back into Vagaro's core platform, sharpening clinical clarity and communication between team members. Because product assignments are tracked automatically and carried through to checkout, treatment documentation stays linked to billing and inventory in real time — helping practices cut down on missed charges and keep inventory numbers accurate. To speed things up further, the new SOAP Notes support reusable dot phrases, letting providers complete detailed notes faster while keeping documentation consistent across the practice. Custom Fields Strengthen Consistency in Patient Records Vagaro's Custom Fields feature has also been expanded, giving med spas more flexibility in how they capture and organize patient information. Practices can use it to collect details like allergies, medications, skin type, and treatment history right on intake and consultation forms, with everything stored directly in the patient profile. That standardization helps keep records consistent across providers and locations, which matters when patients see multiple practitioners over time. It also reduces the odds of important details slipping through the cracks and makes information easier to find and review later. Because Custom Fields can capture key details before an appointment even starts, providers spend less time gathering information during the visit itself — freeing them up to focus on treatment and the overall patient experience. Connecting the Treatment Room to the Business Side Together, the enhanced SOAP Notes and Custom Fields create a more unified workflow — linking patient intake and treatment documentation with product management, injectable tracking, inventory, digital consent forms, and checkout. That gives providers a fuller picture of each treatment and everything tied to it. For multi-location med spas, this can mean more operational consistency across sites; for smaller, independent practices, it's a way to streamline daily workflow without added complexity. Either way, the platform is designed to keep documentation accurate and HIPAA-compliant while supporting the everyday balance between patient care and business needs. "These features are designed to reflect how med spas actually work," said Vagaro CEO Fred Helou. "By connecting what happens in the treatment room directly to inventory and checkout, we're helping practices protect their patients, improve accuracy, save time, and operate more effectively." Vagaro says it plans to keep building out tools tailored specifically to med spas, serving everything from small independent practices to larger enterprise operations. The goal, according to the company, is to help providers deliver strong patient care while giving them the operational tools to grow. With clinical documentation now more tightly connected to business operations, med spas using Vagaro can track treatment information, products, inventory, and checkout through a single, connected system a shift that's likely to matter more as the industry keeps expanding.

data.title: Vagaro's New Med Spa Software Is Real. The Problem for Investors Is That the Company Isn't Public.

data.full_text:
On September 4, Vagaro announced two new features for its medical spa software platform — enhanced SOAP Notes and Custom Fields — and called them a way to turn treatment data into revenue. The announcement sounds like the kind of product ramp that, in a public SaaS company, might move the stock. Vagaro isn't public. It is a private company that has not filed for an IPO, and ordinary retail investors have no ticker to buy.

That alone is the first thing to understand before treating this as an investment lead. But the second thing — why Vagaro is making this move at all, and what the market behind it looks like — is worth the attention. It reveals a real growth story in a niche that sits at the intersection of health care compliance, consumer beauty spending, and small-business software. Understanding it helps you read the sector more clearly, even if you can't own Vagaro itself.

What Vagaro actually built

The announcement centers on two HIPAA-compliant features for the medical spa segment of its platform. SOAP Notes lets providers capture before-and-after photos and mark treatment areas — injection points, laser zones, areas of concern. Practitioners can assign products and quantities to those marked areas, and the data carries automatically through to checkout, inventory, and billing. The idea is to close the gap between what gets done in the treatment room and what gets charged and tracked at the register.

Custom Fields lets med spas collect patient-specific data — allergies, medications, skin type, treatment history — through intake and consultation forms and store it in a central patient profile. Both features are designed to support consistency across providers and locations, reduce missed charges, and improve billing accuracy.

Vagaro said nearly 4 million med spa appointments were scheduled through its platform year-to-date as of the announcement.CEO Fred Helou framed the features as designed to reflect how med spas "actually work," helping practices protect patients, improve accuracy, save time, and operate more effectively.

From a product standpoint, this is a vertical play. Vagaro is trying to stitch together the two halves of a medical spa business: the clinical side with HIPAA documentation requirements, and the service-business side that lives on bookings, retention, and margins. Most platforms were built for one half or the other. A platform that handles both can lock in deeper adoption — and make switching more costly.

The market behind the move

The timing isn't arbitrary. The U.S. medical spa market was valued at roughly $7.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at a mid-teen compound annual rate over the next decade, driven by rising demand for non-invasive aesthetic procedures like Botox, fillers, and laser treatments. The broader global market is estimated to exceed $25 billion.Medical spas operate profit margins of 20% to 25%, with top performers reaching close to 40%.

Within that industry, the medical spa management software segment is smaller but growing fast. Research firms estimate the market at around $295 million in 2023, projected to reach roughly $708 million by 2030 — more than doubling over seven years. As med spas professionalize and adopt compliance requirements, the software they use to run daily operations becomes more mission-critical.

Vagaro itself serves over 100,000 businesses across beauty, wellness, and fitness.Founded in 2009 and based in Pleasanton, California, it raised roughly $163 million in cumulative funding, and achieved a $1 billion unicorn valuation in 2021 when FTV Capital led a funding round.Estimates from private-market trackers put its annual recurring revenue around $66 million in 2024. The company operates in the U.S., Canada, Australia, and the UK.

What investors can't ignore: Vagaro is private

Here is where the story diverges from a typical stock research piece. Vagaro has no ticker symbol. It has not filed for an initial public offering. Shares are not available on public exchanges. Private market platforms like Hiive allow accredited investors to express interest in buying or selling shares, but these transactions are illiquid, subject to company approval, and not accessible to the average retail investor.

There is no public financial filing to examine, no earnings call to parse, no balance sheet to stress-test. The revenue estimates you'll find online — such as the $66 million ARR figure — come from third-party trackers, not company disclosures. The $1 billion to $2.5 billion valuation range cited by private-market databases is inferred from funding rounds and secondary activity, not from a market price.

For a retail investor, that means Vagaro itself is not an actionable investment. Any article that leads with a product announcement from a private company and doesn't address this constraint is skipping the first question you should ask: can I actually invest in this?

What the sector tells you about publicly traded alternatives

The med spa software market is too niche to support many publicly traded pure-players. Vagaro's closest competitor by category is Mindbody — which went public in 2015, was taken private by Vista Equity Partners in 2019 for $1.9 billion, and reportedly plans a return to public markets. No public offering has materialized as of this writing.

That leaves investors looking at broader SaaS comparables in the business-software space — companies that serve appointment-based, service businesses more generally. The dynamics are instructive. Public SaaS multiples have compressed significantly across the board, creating a gap between private-market valuations and public-market pricing. The companies that command premiums in public markets are the ones showing revenue acceleration, expanding margins, and clear paths to free cash flow.

The question for any publicly traded name in this space is the same one that applies to Vagaro's strategy: does the platform's growth story have evidence behind it, in revenue acceleration, customer retention, margin expansion, and whether new product claims convert to measurable demand? Or is the company relying on narrative — that the med spa market is growing, therefore the software built for it must follow?

The investor takeaway

Vagaro's announcement is a genuine product expansion into a clinically regulated, fast-growing vertical. The features address a real operational gap in medical spa management — the friction between clinical documentation and billing — and the strategy of integrating both halves of the business makes sense.

But for the ordinary investor, the practical lesson is different. Product announcements from private companies tell you where the market is heading, not where you can invest. The med spa software market is growing, and the software layer within it is doubling in size over the next five years. That's a sector trend worth watching. Whether it translates into an investment opportunity depends on whether a company in this space goes public and whether, at that point, its growth, margins, and valuation support the multiple the market assigns.

Until then, the most useful thing you can do is pay attention to the dynamics — software adoption in professional services, the growing compliance burden on small health-adjacent businesses, and the competitive positioning of platforms that serve them. These are the variables that will matter when the next company in this space files for an IPO, and they may already be shaping the valuations of the publicly traded SaaS names you can own today.

Yelp Launches the New Yelp Assistant in Spring Release
Yelp launched its Spring Product Release with more than 35 new features and updates, including the new Yelp Assistant, an AI-powered chatbot that delivers instant answers, reliable recommendations, and seamless booking in one conversation.
New integrations with Vagaro, Zocdoc and Calendly expand scheduling capabilities across more categories on Yelp, while enhancements to AI-powered Menu Vision make deciding what to order more visual and engaging. The release also introduces new tools for advertisers, including an AI-powered support chatbot and enhanced advertising tools.
"The new Yelp Assistant is our most significant AI product evolution yet as we reconceive Yelp around instant answers and seamless actions," said Craig Saldanha, chief product officer at Yelp, in a statement. "The experiences and opinions from real people that power every recommendation are what sets Yelp Assistant apart, delivering trustworthy results that help consumers make confident decisions, faster. And for the first time, consumers can seamlessly move from discovery to action in a single conversation with new and enhanced integrations, from booking a table to ordering delivery or scheduling an appointment. As we transform Yelp with AI, this is only the beginning of a more conversational, personalized, and action-oriented Yelp experience."
First introduced to help consumers hire services professionals and answer questions about individual businesses, Yelp Assistant now works across every category on Yelp and is accessible at the center of the app through a new "Assistant" tab on iOS and Android. Powered by hundreds of millions of reviews, photos and detailed business information from the Yelp community, Yelp Assistant can handle complex and highly specific requests and surfaces real user-generated content from first-hand experiences in answers to validate each recommendation.
The new integrations available through Yelp Assistant are now also accessible throughout the Yelp app and include the following:
- Vagaro: Consumers can now book beauty and wellness appointments, such as haircuts, massages, and nail services.
- Zocdoc: Consumers can go from finding to booking a doctor on Yelp.
- Calendly: Service professionals can now connect their Calendly schedules to Yelp, allowing consumers to book consultations and appointments.
Additional features and updates from Yelp's 2026 Spring Product Release include the following:
- Enhanced Menu Vision that now overlays photos of dishes, drinks, and desserts directly over text-based menus when viewed through diners' phone cameras. "Popular" badges call out standout items, and with one tap, consumers can read reviews about the item. Plus, expanded coverage and improved matching accuracy mean more items are recognized across more restaurants. Menu Vision is available on iOS and Android from business media galleries or directly from business pages under the menu section.
- A more personalized and engaging home feed on iOS now surfaces more relevant, tailored content, more updates from people users follow, immersive full-screen videos and smarter nearby recommendations.
- Smarter photo discovery with natural language search within business media galleries.
- AI-powered chat support for advertisers that helps business owners get answers and resolve issues faster. Built with advanced large language models, the chatbot delivers conversational assistance across a wide range of support topics and provides intelligent real-time solutions.
- New tools to help businesses manage leads and optimize their advertising.

The offering enables SMEs in beauty, wellness, and fitness sectors to finance hardware and point-of-sale equipment purchases ranging from USD 500 to USD 10,000, with initial rollout capped at USD 3,000 and payments auto-deducted as a percentage of future revenue. data.full_text: Liberis has launched its first Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) financing product in the US through a partnership with business management platform Vagaro. The initiative aims to expand small business access to financing options directly within the checkout experience. Through this collaboration, Vagaro will integrate Pay with Liberis as Capital for Hardware, allowing small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to finance purchases such as hardware or point-of-sale equipment. Funding will range from USD 500 up to USD 10,000, though the initial rollout is limited to USD 3,000. Payments will be automatically deducted as a set percentage of future revenue, with no penalties for early repayment. Funds are disbursed directly to Vagaro, ensuring a streamlined transaction process for merchants. Addressing financing barriers in niche service sectors The embedded financing tool was developed jointly by Liberis and Vagaro to address specific funding challenges faced by small companies in the beauty, wellness, and fitness sectors. Representatives from Liberis noted that businesses in these industries often struggle with fragmented access to financing and require solutions tailored to their revenue cycles. By embedding the BNPL function within Vagaro’s platform, merchants can manage repayments and access financial information directly through their dashboard. The new offering also connects to Vagaro’s other funding solutions powered by Liberis, including Vagaro Capital. Vagaro officials said the collaboration with Liberis was designed to simplify financing for merchants and reduce barriers to obtaining growth-related funding. The company highlighted that the joint product represents an effort to prioritise merchant needs and improve access to capital. Pay with Liberis is currently available to Vagaro customers in the US, with expansion into additional markets planned for 2026.

data.full_text:
Buy Now, Pay Later product offers finance at check-out, providing funding at the point of need for beauty, health, and wellness SMBs. ATLANTA & LONDON, October 27, 2025--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Liberis, a leading global embedded finance provider, has today announced the U.S. launch of its new Buy Now, Pay Later product, Pay with Liberis. Vagaro, a leading business management platform for the beauty, wellness, and fitness industries, is the first of Liberis’ strategic partners to adopt the new product – which will be offered to their customers as Capital for Hardware. Vagaro’s users can now purchase products or services at checkout and pay through a fixed percentage of future revenue, solving one of SMBs most persistent challenges. This launch establishes Liberis at the forefront of embedded finance innovation, with Liberis and Vagaro collaborating closely on the creation of Pay with Liberis to ensure it was suitable to solve the financing pain points of Vagaro’s users. "Small businesses must navigate a fragmented financing landscape, and businesses within the beauty, health and wellness industries face specific funding issues that require specialised support" says Rob Fairfield, CEO of Liberis. "With Pay with Liberis, we are now able to offer seamless embedded finance offerings that are not only hand-crafted solutions, but actually accelerate growth, as we lead the way in building definitive funding ecosystems." Bespoke offerings for beauty, health and wellness SMBs: Within Vagaro’s platform, Pay with Liberis will be offered to customers as Capital for Hardware, and will offer financing for SMBs from $500 and up to $10,000, although Vagaro’s initial rollout will be capped at $3,000. Pay with Liberis is integrated seamlessly into Vagaro’s checkout process, with merchants able to finance hardware and similar purchases at checkout with funds disbursed directly to Vagaro. Customers can benefit immensely from this integration, with payments automatically split from daily revenue, and no early payment penalties. This product also serves as a gateway to Vagaro’s other financial offerings powered by Liberis, such as Vagaro Capital. Pay with Liberis expands SMB access to growth enabling tools, such as marketing spend and POS hardware, all whilst customers can track repayments and download statements via their dashboard. "When accessing financial services, we want to help our merchants achieve success and remove some of the obstacles they face," says Kerry Melchior, COO of Vagaro. "Collaborating closely with Liberis on Capital for Hardware, we have been able to prioritise our customers’ needs and reinforce our commitment to supporting our merchant community."

Story Continues

Pay with Liberis is now live in the U.S. with plans for expansion into other markets over the course of 2026. About Liberis Liberis is on a mission to unleash the power of small businesses all over the world - delivering the financial products they need to grow through a network of global partners. At its core, Liberis is a technology-driven company, bridging the gap between finance and small businesses. They use data and insights to help partners understand their customers' real time needs and tech to offer tailor-made financial products. Empowering small businesses to grow and keep their independent spirit alive is central to their vision. Since 2007, Liberis has funded over 50,000 small businesses with over $3bn - but they believe there is much more to be done. Learn more about Liberis by visiting: https://www.liberis.com/ About Vagaro Vagaro is the leading salon, spa, and fitness software, serving hundreds of thousands of professionals worldwide. Vagaro simplifies business management, credit card and payment processing, and makes it easy for businesses to grow their clientele on a modern consumer marketplace. Vagaro's a-la-carte options and affordable pricing provide a unique level of scalability, making it suitable for businesses of all sizes, from the solopreneur to enterprise franchises. Simple, innovative, and reliable, Vagaro empowers beauty and wellness professionals to excel in a digital age. Visit Vagaro to learn more.
